newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends down on fund, commercial selling.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends down on fund, commercial selling.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures settled lower Friday, under pressure from modest commercial and fund selling as well as disappointment on news that Egypt will not buy wheat this weekend as some in the trade expected, CBOT floor traders said.
"The market went to session lows when that Egypt story came out," one floor trader said.
Over the past several days, traders had been watching for signs of Egyptian demand. Egypt had been expected to tender for 400,000 to 500,000 tonnes of optional origin wheat, exporters said.
However, on Friday, Samir Shakankiri, vice chairman of the state's General Authority for Supply Commodities, said Egypt will not buy wheat this weekend.
On the day, Cargill sold one million bushels March, Rand Financial sold 1.5 March, and Refco sold 1 million March. Iowa Grain bought 300,000 March and 300,000 July, traders said.
Export sales of 359,500 were said to be supportive to futures. The USDA weekly data came in well above trade estimates for 200,000 to 300,000 tonnes.
Wheat ended down two to 5-1/4 cents per bushel, with March down 5-1/4 at $3.84 and May fell 4-1/2 to $3.64.
The market also fell on news that Sri Lanka did not buy any U.S. in a recent tender, traders said. Instead, it bought 50,000 tonnes from Australia and 50,000 from Argentina, U.S. export sources said.

Reports of heavy cash grain sales added to the weak tone in futures, traders said. Thursday's sharp gains on the Chicago Board of Trade spurred the active farmer selling, especially by those who had been waiting for the new tax year to begin, grain merchandisers said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 14,000 contracts, above the 10,360 traded Thursday, according to the CBOT.
In options trading, E.D. and F. Man bought 100 July $3.60 calls, trade sources said.
